name: US inflation
summary: US CPI 4.0% y/y in September, inside the Watch band; October data due 10 Nov
state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7% in August, inside the 3–4.5% Watch band (BLS via FRED). It has not risen for three straight months on the latest data. Brent was about $98 on 6 Nov, down 6% in a month, easing one source of pressure on the October figure due on 10 Nov.
for_you: Higher prices squeeze real incomes, especially for households spending more on fuel and food.
why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
